title: Chat · Celeriter an clārē? · English → Latin, then Latin only
summary: Too much coffee, a carrot, beautiful birds, and today's chat with ChatGPT: speak fast, or speak clearly? Quotes: Īra furor brevis est (Horace, Letters 1.2), Rem tenē, verba sequentur (Cato the Elder), Sit sermō vester: est, est; nōn, nōn (Matthew 5:37). Each line in English, then in Latin. The whole dialogue 3 times.

title: Chat · Rūfus et cāseus (story, × 3)
summary: Iulia's Saturday: rain, coffee, her dog Rufus, the market, and a stolen cheese. English then Latin, free voices, Latin read from IPA. Quotes: Canis timidus vehementius lātrat quam mordet (Quintus Curtius), Post nūbila Phoebus (old saying). Played 3 times. Latin v said as v.

title: Ladder 5 · ut, nē, cum: the subjunctive pyramid · English → Latin, then Latin only
summary: A pyramid on 5 subjunctive patterns: Rogō ut lentius loquāris · Linguam Latīnam discō, ut tēcum loquar · Caffeam nōn bibō, nē īrātus sim · Cum domum venīrem, fīlius meus clāmābat · Dīc mihi quid hoc significet. Slow steps, plain vs subjunctive contrasts, reviews, and a funny day at the end. English then Latin, free voice (IPA, v as v).

title: Ladder 6 · ut, nē, cum: pyramid 2 · English → Latin, then Latin only
summary: Subjunctive pyramid 2, new sentences: Dīc fīliō meō ut domum veniat · Domum eō, ut cum līberīs cēnem · Timeō nē pīca mē oppugnet · Cum fessus essem, domī mānsī · Scīsne ubi sit cāseus? Slow steps, plain vs subjunctive contrasts, reviews (and pyramid 1's peaks), a funny rainy day at the end. Played twice. Free voice (IPA, v as v).

title: Ladder 7 · Docē mē, ut discam: pyramid 3 · English → Latin, then Latin only
summary: Commands + 'so that…' on how to learn, listen, ask, agree and avoid mistakes: Docē mē, ut discam · Audī mē, ut intellegās · Rogā mē, ut cōgitem · Loquāmur, ut cōnsentiāmus · Prīmum cōgitā, nē errēs. Quotes: Errāre hūmānum est, Docendō discimus. Played twice. Free voice (IPA, v as v).

title: Ladder 8 · 50 new words + 30 hard ones · English → Latin, then Latin only
summary: Road to 2,000, set 1: the next 50 Road words (induō, tunica, sūmō, piscis, mūrus, umbra, collum, iaceō, stēlla, scaena…) in 5 scenes (morning, kitchen, walk, a long night, evening), each word heard 6+ times, plus your 30 stickiest hell words (quoniam, ideō, quidem, quīdam, tamen, īdem, tālis…) in clear sentences. Closing story of the whole day, then a quick-fire list of all 80 words. Free voice (IPA, v as v).

title: Ladder 9 · Admonē mē, quaesō · English → Latin, then Latin only
summary: Iulia's voice (his pick, 28 Oct). Remind me, please; you reminded me; I almost forgot; I will remind you; if you had not reminded me, I would have forgotten.

title: Bible · Matthew 1–5 · English → Latin, then Latin only
summary: The Gospel of Matthew from the start, verse by verse: Douay-Rheims English, then the Latin Vulgate (Clementine). Free voices. About 15 minutes of Latin.

title: Ladder 10 · Conventus dē conventibus (the meeting about meetings) · English → Latin, then Latin only
summary: A funny pyramid: Gaius calls a meeting to cut meetings. "I will speak briefly" (then an hour), ut + subjunctive requests that crack, nisi … loquerētur, iam domī essem, quoniam nēmō audit, ego quidem tacēbō, cum … fīnītus esset. Iulia's voice.

title: Ladder 11 · Tessera (the password) · English → Latin, then Latin only
summary: Monday at the office: Quintus from IT makes the password rules (must be changed every day, longer than the old one, a number, a sign, not your dog). Gerundive, comparatives, relative clauses, future perfect, perfect passive. Iulia's voice.

title: Ladder 12 · Analysis (the analysis) · English → Latin, then Latin only
summary: Gaius wants a perfect analysis of the new product "Speed" before Friday, but every time he consults his new calendar the deadline moves closer, until Marcus discovers the product IS the calendar, and it is too fast.

title: Ladder 16 · Epistulae dē cāseō (letters about a cheese)
summary: Ten letters between two Roman friends: Marcus in noisy Rome begs Lucius for his famous cheese; a procession, a letter carrier who smells of cheese, well-mannered robbers who send a thank-you letter, and a neighbour who guards the cheese by eating it. English → Latin, then the Latin twice. Iulia's voice.

title: Ladder 17 · Caesar et pīrātae (Caesar and the pirates)
summary: 75 BC, a true story (Plutarch, Suetonius): pirates seize young Caesar off Miletus. Marcus writes from the pirates' island, Lucius from the harbour of Miletus, collecting the ransom Caesar himself raised from 20 to 50 talents. Poems, 'barbarians', a sworn promise. English → Latin, then the Latin twice. Iulia's voice.

title: Leō Parvus · 2 · In culīnā (in the kitchen, for little ones)
summary: For Gus: Leo the little lion asks Daddy for things in the kitchen. English then Latin: Lac, quaesō! Dā mihi aquam, quaesō! Salsīciae! Plūs, quaesō! Grātiās, Pater! Lūde mēcum, quaesō!
